skills.name: collective-action
skills.description: Reference card for collective action problems: free-riding, selective incentives, and how groups organize (or fail to) under shared goals. Load when mapping who benefits, who pays, and who can veto or free-ride.

skills.name: confirmation-bias
skills.description: Reference card for confirmation bias: seeking, interpreting, and remembering evidence in ways that favor an already preferred conclusion. Load when auditing search strategy, counter-evidence, and motivated updating.

skills.name: macro-scan
skills.description: Break a situation, industry, or system into structure: actors, incentives, constraints, and trajectories. Use when a complex picture needs a macro/system read before judging or deciding.

skills.name: metacognition-audit
skills.description: Audit a line of thinking: expose biases, blind spots, and evidence gaps instead of polishing conclusions. Use after a conclusion forms and before it ships, when thought quality matters.

skills.name: path-dependence
skills.description: Reference card for path dependence: how early choices and increasing returns lock systems into trajectories that are costly to reverse. Load when mapping lock-in, sunk commitments, or why "better" options stay unused.

skills.name: personal-anchor
skills.description: Place a personal situation on historical and social coordinates: which curve you are on, which stratum you stand on. Use for long-horizon choices—career, city, direction—when orientation matters more than pep talk.

skills.name: prospect-theory
skills.description: Reference card for prospect theory: reference points, loss aversion, and probability weighting that shape choices under risk. Load when auditing framing, asymmetric risk attitudes, or over-weighted small probabilities.

skills.name: social-stratification
skills.description: Reference card for social stratification: layered positions in education, occupation, wealth, status, and networks. Load when locating a person or group on structural coordinates without reducing them to a slogan.
